quizzes.stem: Scenario S3, multi-agent research system. A web-search subagent's service call times out now and then. Each time, the subagent reports a failure to the coordinator, which delegates the whole task again. Runs are slow, and the coordinator's context fills with repeated failure reports. What should change?

options.a: Let the coordinator make every retry itself, since only it sees the whole picture of the run
options.b: Let the worker retry the transient fault itself, passing up only what it cannot resolve
options.c: Raise the subagent's timeout far enough that a failure can no longer occur
options.d: Stop retrying anywhere, so that the user decides about each failure

explanation.b: The subagent holds the query and the work done, so it retries what is transient and reports only what survives.
explanation.a: Ruled out because passing failures up has the cost that "the coordinator's context fills with failure reports" and the decision is made "without the subagent's detail".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a timeout is the example of a "transient failure", which is retried "a bounded number of times" and not designed away.
explanation.d: Ruled out because it would hand the user each transient failure, when "a transient failure, a timeout or a brief outage, is the subagent's to retry".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3, multi-agent research system. A document-analysis subagent opens forty files, fails to open two, and ends with the sentence "Analysis finished." The coordinator's report then claims complete coverage. Which change fits best?

options.a: Have the coordinator read the subagent's tool calls afterwards to find the files that failed
options.b: Raise the coordinator's turn limit so that it can inspect more of the run
options.c: Instruct the worker to close with a structured account of what it read and missed
options.d: Run the subagent twice and compare its two final sentences against each other

explanation.c: Only the final message reaches the parent, so the structure has to be requested there.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "intermediate tool calls and results stay inside the subagent; only its final message returns to the parent".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the coordinator has nothing more to inspect: "Everything the subagent did in between" stays inside it.
explanation.d: Ruled out because two runs of the same instruction return the same kind of sentence, and "the structure has to be asked for in the subagent's instructions".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3, multi-agent research system. A subagent returns an empty list when its lookup service times out, and the coordinator's report says that the topic has nothing in the sources. What fixes the cause?

options.a: Treat every blank answer as a failure and send it back for another attempt
options.b: Mark the timeout as a typed failure, distinct from a genuine absence of matches
options.c: Remove the topics with no results from the report so that no false claim remains in it
options.d: Have the coordinator rerun any topic whose report says that nothing was found

explanation.b: A failure and a valid empty result are different values with different handling.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Treat the empty result as a failure, and the system retries a search that already worked".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A report that quietly omits a topic is saying something false by leaving it out".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A search that runs and finds nothing has succeeded", so rerunning it repeats a finished job and leaves the timeout unreported.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3, multi-agent research system. A synthesis step merges findings on six topics. Two sources were unreachable, and one search found nothing. The report reads as a complete survey. What should the step add?

options.a: A confidence score for the whole report, shown as a single number between zero and one
options.b: A line saying that some sources may be unavailable at the moment of writing
options.c: A note that sorts subjects into evidenced and unevidenced, with the cause of each gap
options.d: A longer introduction describing in detail how the survey was carried out and by whom

explanation.c: The note compares what was planned with what happened, topic by topic.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the note is "the place where the system's own plan is compared with what happened", and a single score compares nothing.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a line like that "names no topic and no cause, so no reader can act on it".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A reader who sees a confident survey with a hole in it learns about the hole later and from someone else".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3, multi-agent research system. One of four research subagents is refused access to a source, and the coordinator cancels the run and tells the user that it failed. Which handling fits?

options.a: Retry the refused one again and again until the door finally opens, then continue
options.b: Ask the user to restart the whole run after the source has been fixed
options.c: Fill the closed gap with a plausible summary drawn from the model's own general knowledge
options.d: Carry on with the other three and log the closed topic as a gap, with a way to reopen it

explanation.d: Terminating on one failure wastes the other work, and a refusal is recorded as a gap with the way to get access.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "a permission error or an invalid query fails again the same way, and the subagent reports it at once".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "terminating on a single failure throws away the work of the other subagents".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the plan for a failure with nothing to try is "Say what is missing, and do not guess".

quizzes.stem: A subagent stops at its maxTurns limit after doing good work. What does the parent receive, and what can it do?

options.a: An error that discards the output, so that the task has to be started again
options.b: Nothing at all until the user raises the limit and runs it again
options.c: The output so far, flagged as partial, and the option to resume it later
options.d: The output with no flag at all, which looks like a finished answer

explanation.c: The output comes back marked as partial, and a custom subagent keeps its history so that it can be resumed.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "the parent receives its output flagged as partial", and nothing is discarded.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Resuming is cheaper than starting a fresh subagent on the same task when the work so far is good", and no one has to rerun it.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the marker exists so that "Claude knows the run is unfinished".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3, multi-agent research system. During a run on one subject, a subagent's source stops answering after supplying three of the ten items that were expected. What should the coordinator do with the three?

options.a: Discard the three, since a partial answer is judged too unreliable to use at all
options.b: Present the three to readers as the subject's complete answer
options.c: Wait and rerun the lookup until all ten items have arrived
options.d: Use them, mark the topic as partly evidenced and say what is lacking

explanation.d: The three results are kept and labelled, with the gap stated.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Discarding them wastes work the subagent did".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "presenting them as the full answer is the silent suppression of page 1 in another form".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "An alternative is tried once, within the bounded rounds of module 46, and a second failure becomes a gap".
